title: keyof, typeof, and Indexed Access Types

options.text: A union of T's property names (keys)
A union of T's value types
The number of keys in T

questions.explanation: keyof T is the union of T's property names. For { id: number; name: string } it's 'id' | 'name'.

questions.prompt: What does `typeof value` mean in a type position (versus in an expression)?

options.text: The same thing in both places
In a type position it's the static type of the value; in an expression it's a runtime type string like 'string'
It's invalid in a type position

questions.explanation: In a type position, typeof is a type query giving the value's static type. In an expression it's the runtime typeof operator returning a string.

questions.prompt: How do you get the type of the `name` property of `User`?
questions.explanation: Indexed access User['name'] looks up the type of the name property.

questions.prompt: To turn `const roles = ['a','b'] as const` into the union 'a' | 'b', write (typeof roles)[______]. (one word)
questions.explanation: (typeof roles)[number] indexes the tuple type by number, yielding the union of its element types.

questions.prompt: Why is it `keyof typeof config` rather than `keyof config` for a value `config`?

options.text: keyof needs a type; typeof config converts the value to its type first, then keyof takes its keys

questions.explanation: keyof operates on a type. For a value you first apply typeof to get its type, then keyof to get its keys.

options.text: A union of all the value types in User

questions.explanation: Indexing a type by all of its keys (keyof User) yields a union of all the property value types.
